data.title: Manipulated Video or Audio of Organisation Representatives
data.summary:
Video or audio purporting to show executives or spokespeople making statements they did
not make was circulated in support of the campaign.
data.description:
Synthetic audio is the more dangerous of the two in practice. It is cheaper to produce,
far harder to assess, and travels through channels — voicemail, meeting recordings,
forwarded clips — where no provenance signal exists and where recipients act on it
directly.

The operational risk is not only reputational. Synthetic voice of a named executive is
the same artefact used for payment fraud, and a campaign that has produced one has
produced the input for the other. Treat the discovery as relevant to the finance process
as well as to communications.

Short clips of public figures are the usual target, because training material is
abundant. Executives who speak publicly are therefore the most exposed, which is worth
stating plainly to them.
data.recommendation:
* Treat a synthetic voice artefact as a fraud indicator as well as an influence one, and
  brief finance and executive assistants accordingly.
* Require out-of-band verification for any instruction received by voice, independent of
  how familiar the voice is.
* Publish official recordings through a channel the organisation controls, so there is an
  authoritative version to compare against.
data.short_recommendation: Treat synthetic voice as a fraud indicator; verify out of band.
